bug_semantics: Bandit.HTTP2.Frame.deserialize/2 in lib/bandit/http2/frame.ex rejected SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE violations only in a clause that also required payload::binary-size(length), so the 24-bit length field was not checked until the entire announced body was already in the connection buffer. Incomplete oversized frames returned {:more, msg} and the HTTP/2 handler kept concatenating bytes. An unauthenticated HTTP/2 peer could announce length=0xFFFFFF (~16 MiB) on a connection that had negotiated the RFC 9113 default 16384-byte max_frame_size and force the server to buffer far beyond the agreed budget (memory-exhaustion DoS / CWE-770). No Plug or application auth is involved; the bug is in the framing layer before any request handling.
flaw_origin: The intended max-frame-size control was first written in f00dd69a5b2a4863be585907acd853c4ffd41399 ('Raise error when receiving oversized frame'). That commit added the max_frame_size argument and a when length > max_frame_size error clause, but the error clause still pattern-matched _payload::binary-size(length), so the guard could not fire until the body had been fully received. Immediate parent c7bfd639f8f07971090a6b8c009a8067589b9f44 had deserialize/1 with the same body-bearing binary match and {:more, msg} fallback, but no max_frame_size parameter or size-error clause. Later refactors (including ba755c03 / fff06efe) preserved the late-check shape. 1e8e55966da9129016b73d32f0e1df4630e3b463 is the first commit that evaluates length from the 9-byte header alone.

reasoning: Vulnerability is a late SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE check: both the accept clause (length <= max_frame_size) and the reject clause (length > max_frame_size) required the full payload binary, so an oversized announced length never matched until the body arrived and the connection layer kept buffering via {:more, msg}. That is CWE-770 memory exhaustion, confirmed by the GHSA PoC and still PUBLISHED on CVE.org. The smallest commit that first wrote the flawed size-limit mechanism is f00dd69a5b2a4863be585907acd853c4ffd41399: it introduced max_frame_size into deserialize/2 and the Payload size too large error clause while keeping the body-size pattern on that clause. The parent lacks that clause entirely (introducer_parent_absent=true). Earlier commits 2b447817/69042303 created the body-bearing parser and {:more} buffering without any max_frame_size cap; they are not this CVE's BIC because the advisory's defective control is the late check, which did not exist until f00dd69, matching the CNA git start f00dd69 and Hex start 0.3.6. The 2024 H2 refactor/revert/reintroduce did not originate the late-check. Fix 1e8e559 is the direct patch landing on main (single parent; fork second parent not in this clone) and is contained in tag 1.11.0.
